MOLECULES.name: 2-Butanol
MOLECULES.note: Ethyl outranks methyl: the first carbon tie is broken by C versus H in the next layer.

MOLECULES.name: Lactic acid
MOLECULES.note: In CO₂H, the carbonyl oxygen is counted twice for this comparison, giving [O, O, O].

MOLECULES.name: Bromochlorofluoromethane
MOLECULES.note: Here, the four directly attached atoms differ. Atomic number alone resolves the order.

MOLECULES.name: 2-Propanol
MOLECULES.note: The two methyl groups remain tied. There is no unique set of four priorities and no R/S assignment at this carbon.

MOLECULES.name: 2-Aminobutanoic acid
MOLECULES.note: N outranks C. Between the carbon groups, [O, O, O] outranks [C, H, H]. This is the neutral structural formula.

MISSIONS.title: 1 · Find the stereocenter
MISSIONS.q: At C2 of 2-butanol, the attached groups are OH, H, CH₃, and CH₂CH₃. Which conclusion is correct?
options: C2 is a stereocenter; the molecule is chiral.
C2 is not a stereocenter because two groups start with C.
The molecule must have positive optical rotation.
MISSIONS.hint: Compare whole groups, not just their first atom.
MISSIONS.explain: CH₃ and CH₂CH₃ are different groups. This tetrahedral carbon has four different substituents, making it a stereocenter and this one-center molecule chiral.

MISSIONS.title: 2 · Recognize a repeated group
options: The O atom has the highest atomic number.
The central carbon has two equivalent methyl groups.
The molecule has no carbon–carbon bonds.
MISSIONS.hint: List the four groups on the carbon carrying OH.
MISSIONS.explain: Its central carbon is attached to OH, H, CH₃, and CH₃. The two methyl groups are equivalent, so that carbon is not a stereocenter and the mirror images are superimposable.

MISSIONS.title: 3 · Break a CIP tie
MISSIONS.q: Which is the correct priority order at C2 of 2-butanol, from highest (1) to lowest (4)?
MISSIONS.hint: O outranks C. Compare [C,H,H] with [H,H,H] to break the carbon tie.
MISSIONS.explain: OH is first and H is fourth. Ethyl outranks methyl because [C,H,H] beats [H,H,H] at the first difference.

MISSIONS.title: 4 · Handle a carbonyl
MISSIONS.q: In lactic acid, compare the CO₂H and CH₃ groups attached to the stereocenter. Which ranks higher?
options: CH₃, because it has more H atoms.
Whichever group is on a wedge.
MISSIONS.hint: For this comparison, count the carbonyl oxygen twice.
MISSIONS.explain: Both groups first attach through C. CO₂H supplies [O,O,O] in the next comparison, while CH₃ supplies [H,H,H]. Drawing direction does not affect CIP priority.

MISSIONS.title: 5 · Assign R/S with H away
MISSIONS.q: Assign the configuration of this 2-butanol model. In the starting view, H points directly away, behind C*. Reset the question view if you have rotated it.
options: Cannot be assigned from this drawing
MISSIONS.hint: OH = 1, CH₂CH₃ = 2, CH₃ = 3, H = 4. With H away, read 1 → 2 → 3 directly.
MISSIONS.explain: The path OH → CH₂CH₃ → CH₃ runs clockwise. Since H points away, the configuration is R.

MISSIONS.title: 6 · Assign R/S with H toward
MISSIONS.q: Assign the configuration of this 2-butanol model. In the starting view, H points directly toward you. Reset the question view if you have rotated it.
MISSIONS.hint: Trace OH → CH₂CH₃ → CH₃, then reverse the result because H points toward you.
MISSIONS.explain: The starting view has a clockwise OH → ethyl → methyl path. H points toward you, so reverse it: S.

MISSIONS.title: 7 · Rotate without inverting
MISSIONS.q: You rotate an R molecule in space without exchanging groups or breaking bonds. What happens to its configuration?
options: It changes to S after a 180° turn.
It depends on which group looks highest on the screen.
MISSIONS.hint: A new viewing direction does not rearrange the attached groups.
MISSIONS.explain: Proper rotation preserves configuration. Reorient group 4 away before interpreting the new drawing.

MISSIONS.title: 8 · Identify an enantiomer pair
MISSIONS.hint: Compare both centers, then check whether whole-molecule symmetry makes the pair identical.
MISSIONS.explain: (2R,3R) and (2S,3S) are distinct mirror images. Both configurations are inverted, and neither structure is meso.

MISSIONS.title: 9 · Identify diastereomers
MISSIONS.hint: C2 stays R while C3 changes. Are these whole molecules mirror images?
MISSIONS.explain: (2R,3R) and (2R,3S) have the same connectivity but are neither identical nor mirror images. They are diastereomers.

MISSIONS.title: 10 · Find the meso exception
options: Enantiomers because both labeled centers change.
Diastereomers because there are two centers.
Identical: two descriptions of the meso compound.
MISSIONS.hint: The two ends are both CH₃. Compare equivalent atoms, allowing rotation and conformational changes.
MISSIONS.explain: (2R,3S) and (2S,3R) represent the same meso compound. The identical ends permit the two central carbons to exchange roles during superposition.

MISSIONS.title: 11 · Check connectivity first
MISSIONS.q: 2-Butanol, CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₂–CH₃, and butan-1-ol, HO–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃, have the same formula. What is their relationship?
MISSIONS.hint: Which carbon is bonded to O in each compound?
MISSIONS.explain: Their atoms are connected differently: OH is attached to C2 versus C1. They are constitutional isomers, so an enantiomer/diastereomer comparison does not apply.

MISSIONS.title: 12 · Separate R/S from optical rotation
MISSIONS.q: You know that a pure enantiomer has R configuration. What can you conclude about its optical rotation sign?
options: R/S alone does not determine the sign.
It must be zero because R means racemic.
MISSIONS.hint: Configuration and measured optical rotation are different descriptions.
MISSIONS.explain: R describes spatial configuration under the CIP rules. It does not specify (+) or (−); the rotation sign requires experimental information.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows bromochlorofluoromethane. What is the configuration of the highlighted carbon?
options: Neither: this carbon is not a stereocenter
It depends on how the model is rotated
QUESTIONS.why: Priorities follow atomic number: Br > Cl > F > H. Turn the model so the C–H bond points away from you. Tracing Br → Cl → F then runs clockwise, so the center is R. Rotating a molecule never changes its configuration.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows one enantiomer of butan-2-ol. What is the configuration of the highlighted carbon?
options: Neither: this carbon is not a stereocenter
It depends on how the model is rotated
QUESTIONS.why: Priorities: OH > CH2CH3 > CH3 > H. Ethyl outranks methyl because its first carbon carries (C,H,H) rather than (H,H,H). With H pointing away, OH → ethyl → methyl runs counterclockwise, so the center is S.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows ibuprofen with four carbons numbered 1 to 4. Which numbered carbon is a stereocenter?
QUESTIONS.why: Carbon 3 carries four different groups: H, CH3, COOH and the aromatic ring. Carbon 1 carries two identical methyl groups, carbon 2 carries two hydrogens, and carbon 4 (the carboxyl carbon) is sp2 with only three attached groups. The model is (S)-ibuprofen, the active enantiomer.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows menthol. How many stereocenters does it contain?
QUESTIONS.why: Three ring carbons each carry four different groups: the carbon bearing OH, the carbon bearing the isopropyl group, and the carbon bearing the methyl group. The isopropyl CH is not a stereocenter because it carries two identical methyl groups. Natural (−)-menthol is (1R,2S,5R).

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows a stereoisomer of 3-methylpent-2-ene. What is the configuration of the double bond?
options: Neither: this alkene has no E/Z isomers
It cannot be assigned, because E/Z needs a hydrogen on each alkene carbon
QUESTIONS.why: On C2 the higher-priority group is CH3 (over H). On C3 it is ethyl (over methyl). Those two groups lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so the alkene is E. The E/Z system works for any alkene whose two carbons each carry two different groups.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows a stereoisomer of 1-bromo-2-chloro-1-fluoroethene. What is the configuration of the double bond?
options: Neither: this alkene has no E/Z isomers
It cannot be assigned, because no two substituents are the same
QUESTIONS.why: On C1, Br outranks F. On C2, Cl outranks H. Br and Cl sit on the same side of the double bond, so the alkene is Z. Cis/trans would be ambiguous here, which is exactly the case E/Z was designed for.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows a stereoisomer of hepta-2,4-diene. What are the configurations of its two double bonds?
QUESTIONS.why: Number from the methyl end nearest the diene, so C2=C3 is the double bond next to the terminal CH3 and C4=C5 is the one next to the ethyl group. At C2=C3 the higher-priority groups (CH3 and the rest of the chain) are on opposite sides: E. At C4=C5 they are on the same side: Z.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows the amino acid L-cysteine. What is the configuration of the highlighted α-carbon?
options: Neither: this carbon is not a stereocenter
It depends on how the model is rotated
QUESTIONS.why: Priorities: NH2 > CH2SH > COOH > H. The CH2SH carbon carries (S,H,H) and the COOH carbon carries (O,O,O). Comparison stops at the first difference, and S outranks O. That swap makes L-cysteine R, although most other L-amino acids are S.

QUESTIONS.prompt: Molecules A and B are both 2-chlorobutane. What is the relationship between them?
QUESTIONS.why: The connectivity is the same, but A is (S) and B is (R). Opposite configuration at the only stereocenter makes them non-superimposable mirror images: enantiomers.

QUESTIONS.prompt: Molecules A and B are both 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane. What is the relationship between them?
QUESTIONS.why: A is (2S,3S) and B is (2R,3S). The configuration differs at the carbon bearing Br but matches at the carbon bearing Cl. Stereoisomers that are not mirror images are diastereomers.

QUESTIONS.prompt: Molecules A and B are both 2-bromobutane. What is the relationship between them?
QUESTIONS.why: Both are (S)-2-bromobutane. They differ only by rotation about the C2–C3 single bond (anti and gauche conformations) and by their orientation in space. Conformers interconvert freely and are the same compound.

QUESTIONS.prompt: Molecules A and B both have the formula C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>11</sub>Cl. What is the relationship between them?
QUESTIONS.why: A is 2-chloropentane and B is 1-chloro-2-methylbutane. The atoms are connected in a different order, so they are constitutional isomers. Check connectivity first: terms such as enantiomer and diastereomer only apply when the connectivity is identical.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows L-threonine (2-amino-3-hydroxybutanoic acid). What are the configurations of C2, which bears NH<sub>2</sub>, and C3, which bears OH?
QUESTIONS.why: At C2: NH2 > COOH > CH(OH)CH3 > H, which gives S. COOH (O,O,O) outranks C3 (O,C,H). At C3: OH > C2 > CH3 > H, which gives R.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows one stereoisomer of tartaric acid. Which statement describes it?
options: It is a meso compound: achiral, even though it has two stereocenters
It is chiral and has a non-superimposable mirror image
It is achiral because it has no stereocenters
QUESTIONS.why: C2 and C3 are both stereocenters and carry the same four groups, but with opposite configurations (R and S). Rotate about the central C–C bond and the two halves become mirror images of each other, so the molecule is superimposable on its own mirror image. A single compound cannot be a racemic mixture, which is a 50:50 mix of two enantiomers.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows one stereoisomer of 2,3-dibromobutane. How many stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane exist in total?
QUESTIONS.why: Two stereocenters allow at most 22 = 4 stereoisomers. Here both centers carry the same four groups, so (2R,3S) and (2S,3R) are one meso compound. The total is three: (2R,3R), (2S,3S) and meso. The model shown is (2S,3S).

QUESTIONS.prompt: Molecule B is the mirror image of molecule A, a stereoisomer of 2,3-dibromobutane. What is the relationship between A and B?
QUESTIONS.why: A is the meso isomer: its two stereocenters carry the same groups with opposite configurations. A meso compound is superimposable on its mirror image, so A and B are the same compound. Mirror images are enantiomers only when the molecule is chiral.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows a stereoisomer of 1,3-dimethylcyclohexane. Which description is correct?
QUESTIONS.why: Both methyl groups are on the same face of the ring (both equatorial in this chair), so the isomer is cis. A mirror plane passes through C2 and C5, which makes it a meso compound: C1 and C3 are stereocenters (R and S), yet the molecule is achiral. The trans isomer is the chiral one.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows the chair conformation of cis-1-tert-butyl-4-methylcyclohexane. Which positions do the two substituents occupy?
QUESTIONS.why: A cis-1,4-disubstituted chair always has one axial and one equatorial substituent. The bulky tert-butyl group takes the equatorial position to avoid 1,3-diaxial strain, which leaves the methyl group axial, pointing straight up or down parallel to the ring axis.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows one enantiomer of carvone. What is the configuration of the highlighted carbon?
options: Neither: this carbon is not a stereocenter
It depends on how the model is rotated
QUESTIONS.why: The isopropenyl carbon (C,C,C) ranks first. The two ring CH2 groups tie at (C,H,H), so move one atom further: the CH2 next to C=O leads to a carbon with (O,O,C), which beats the (C,C,H) found on the alkene side. Order: isopropenyl > CH2C=O > CH2CH= > H, which gives S. This is (S)-(+)-carvone from caraway. Its enantiomer smells of spearmint.

QUESTIONS.prompt: The model shows penta-2,3-diene, an allene. Which statement is correct?
options: It is chiral, even though it has no stereocenter
It is achiral, because it has no stereocenter
It is achiral, because the molecule is planar
It is chiral, because the central carbon is a stereocenter
QUESTIONS.why: The two π bonds of an allene are perpendicular, so the H and CH<sub>3</sub> on one end lie in a plane at 90° to those on the other end. With two different groups on each end, the molecule has no mirror plane and is not superimposable on its mirror image. This is axial chirality: a stereocenter is sufficient for chirality in many molecules, but it is not required.
